title: Vijay Sethupathi's 'Maharaja' Heads to Hollywood in Landmark Tamil Remake Deal
excerpt: The 2024 neo-noir thriller will be the first Tamil film officially remade by a major Hollywood studio, after its ₹91.65 crore run in China caught the attention of an American agency.
body:
• The producers of Maharaja announced on September 16 that the 2024 Tamil thriller will be remade in Hollywood by a major studio, billing it as the first Tamil film to get an American remake.
  • Producer Sudhan Sundaram told The Times of India that a Hollywood agency approached the makers after the film earned ₹91.65 crore in China and built an international audience on streaming.
  • The agency is lining up an A-list star, with production targeted for next year; social media has floated Matthew McConaughey for Vijay Sethupathi's role, but no casting or studio has been officially confirmed.
  • The original grossed ₹199.20 crore worldwide and streams on Netflix; actor Aamir Khan has separately acquired the Hindi remake rights, according to Livemint.

The 2024 Tamil neo-noir thriller Maharaja is going to Hollywood. The film's producers announced on Wednesday that an English-language remake is in development at a major studio, a deal they described as the first of its kind for Tamil cinema.

Context & Background

Directed by Nithilan Saminathan and produced by The Route, Think Studios and Passion Studios, Maharaja was released in June 2024 and marked Vijay Sethupathi's 50th film as a lead actor. The film opens with an odd police complaint: a barber named Maharaja reports the theft of his dustbin, which he calls Lakshmi. What begins as an almost comic misunderstanding unravels into a much darker revenge story, told in a non-linear structure that critics singled out as the film's defining strength. Anurag Kashyap played the antagonist, with Mamta Mohandas, Natty Subramaniam, Sachana Namidass and Abhirami in the cast.

According to trade website Sacnilk, Maharaja earned ₹72.43 crore net at the Indian box office and ₹199.20 crore worldwide, emerging as one of the highest-grossing Tamil releases of 2024. It found an unexpected second life in China, where it grossed about ₹91.65 crore, and drew a global audience on Netflix, where it is currently streaming.

Impact & Analysis

What makes the deal unusual is its direction. The makers were not shopping the film internationally; a Hollywood agency approached producer Sudhan Sundaram after the China and streaming numbers landed on its radar. That reverses the usual flow, in which Indian producers option Hollywood properties for local remakes. Official Hollywood adaptations of Indian films remain rare enough that the producers are calling this a first for Tamil cinema, though neither the studio nor the cast has been named publicly.

"₹91 crore success in China prompted an agency to approach them for remake rights. They are now trying to set up the project with an A-list star. The film is likely to go on floors by next year."

— Sudhan Sundaram, Producer, via The Times of India

The interest also reflects how non-linear, twist-driven storytelling has become Indian cinema's most exportable asset. Where the previous decade's crossover hits leaned on spectacle, Maharaja travelled on the strength of its screenplay — exactly the kind of high-concept crime narrative Hollywood has been importing from other industries for years.

Diaspora Angle

For the Tamil diaspora in the US, UK and Canada, Maharaja is already a familiar title — many watched it on Netflix rather than in theaters. A Hollywood remake would complete an unusual arc: a Tamil film that bypassed the diaspora's usual Bollywood-centric distribution channels, found its audience on streaming and in China, and is now being re-imported to American screens in English. If the casting speculation is anything to go by, Sethupathi's barber could soon be an Oscar winner.

What's Next

Sundaram says the agency is now working to attach an A-list actor, with production eyed for next year. Reports in recent days have linked Matthew McConaughey to the lead role, but the producer has been careful to keep that at arm's length. Separately, Aamir Khan has reportedly acquired the rights to remake Maharaja in Hindi, meaning the thriller could be re-made in two industries at once.

"Maybe McConaughey is one of the stars they are talking to, but only the agency will be able to confirm."

— Sudhan Sundaram, Producer, via The Times of India
